newsitem.title: USA: Ford won't take non-union seats from Johnson.
newsitem.headline: Ford won't take non-union seats from Johnson.

text.p: Ford Motor Co said Tuesday it told the United Auto Workers union it will not accept seats made by non-union workers at Johnson Control Inc plants.
More than 500 UAW-represented workers at Johnson plants in Plymouth and Oberlin, Ohio, struck the facilities Tuesday morning after talks broke down on a new contract.

Johnson had said it would continue making seats at the plants by using temporary and permanent replacement workers, if necessary. But Ford officials told the UAW it would not accept the seats, said Ford spokesman Bill Carroll.
"We're not accepting seats made by the non-union employees of Johnson Controls," Carroll said.
Ford's decision could hurt its own production of the Expedition, a full-size sport/utility that is currently one of the automaker's most popular -- and most profitable -- vehicles.

The Plymouth plant supplies final seat assembly on Expeditions made at Ford's Michigan Truck plant in nearby Wayne, Mich. Production of Ford's F-Series pickup trucks, which are also made at Michigan Truck, has not been affected because it uses seats made by Ford's Chesterfield, Mich., trim plant, said Carroll.

Ford is continuing to produce the Expeditions, using seats it already had in inventory, Carroll said. If those ran out, Ford would still make the vehicles without seats and park them nearby. Ford has been building the Expeditions at a rate of 42 an hour, up from 37 when production first started last summer.
The Oberlin plant makes seats for Ford's Econoline full-size van.
